info.title: AeroCore Update Server API
info.description:
Contract between an update server and a GCS node that pulls updates from it. The node identifies itself (serial, platform, installed version, channel) and the server decides what it should be running, which enables staged rollout, per-serial pinning and stopping a bad release without touching the fleet.

Normative prose, the signature payload definition and a reference implementation: docs/update-server-api.md.

The downloaded body is an ordinary component-aware OTA package as produced by scripts/package_update_bundle.sh — this protocol introduces no new package format.

servers.description: Operator-configured base URL; the node appends the paths below.

get.summary: Ask what this device should be running
get.description:
Safe, idempotent and cacheable — poll freely within the etiquette in the prose doc (suggested: hourly, jittered, honouring Retry-After).

Return `{"update_available": false}` — not a 404 — both when the node is current and when the server is deliberately withholding an update from this device (paused rollout, pinned serial). The node treats the two identically.

parameters.name: serial
parameters.description: The node's serial, from link.serial in core.json. Identifies the device for targeting.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The node's platform, as stamped into its runtime manifest.json. Match exactly; do not parse apart.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Currently installed core version. Compared component-wise as integers, never lexically.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: The node's system, from its runtime manifest.json - which product this device is. Omitted entirely by a build that was not stamped. An unrecognised name is not an error: the server offers no update (204) and records the node for an operator to place.

parameters.name: plugins
parameters.description: Comma-separated Name@version list, so the server can offer plugin-only updates.

200.description: Either an offered update or a statement that none applies.

value.notes: Adds ZMQ bus self-description. Fixes config reset on OTA.

current.summary: Node is current, or the rollout is withheld from it

get.description:
Body is a component-aware OTA package (.tar.gz).

Content-Length is mandatory and must be exact — the node uses it for a real progress percentage and to reject a truncated body early, so chunked transfer without a length degrades both.

Range support only needs the open-ended `bytes=N-` form, which is all a resuming download uses. Multi-range is not required; reject it with 416 if unimplemented.

With no `platform`, serve the fleet catalog artifact (all platforms in one). With `platform`, serve the slim artifact for it.

Components a bundle may carry: `core` (binary + webui/docs, restart), `plugin` (per-platform, hot-loaded), `config` (slim value-only param payload per target; plugin params apply live, core params on next restart). Locked/readonly params are skipped by the node rather than overwritten. Unknown component types are skipped, not fatal.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The node's platform. REQUIRED — it selects the slim artifact built for it, and validates that a fleet artifact actually covers it. A package with no matching variant is 404 rather than bytes the node would install nothing from.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: Which product these bytes are for. REQUIRED. The server puts it into every url it hands out, so a node returns it without knowing the concept exists. Absent is 400; naming another system is 404, indistinguishable from a version that does not exist.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Resume offset. Only `bytes=N-` need be supported.

206.description: Partial body, in response to a Range request.

post.summary: Report the outcome of an update (optional)
post.description:
Recommended, not required — a minimal server may omit it and return 404. Without it you cannot tell a rollout is failing until someone phones in.

The node treats any failure here as non-fatal and does not retry: reporting must never block an update.

get.description: No auth required. Lets a node — and your monitoring — distinguish "server unreachable" from "no update available", which are very different operationally.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Shared key, stored as a locked param in the node's core.json. Keeps scanners out and gives per-fleet revocation. NOT an identity proof: over plain HTTP anyone who reads core.json or sniffs the wire has it. The manifest signature, not this key, is what protects package integrity.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: ETag from a previous response; a match yields 304 with no body.

ETag.description: Must be a function of everything that affects the response — at minimum version, platform and channel — so a rollout change invalidates it.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. The node backs off on this.

Version.description: Dotted numeric MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Compared component-wise as INTEGERS with the shorter side zero-padded, so 0.9.0 < 0.10.0. Never compare these as strings — lexically "0.9.0" > "0.10.0", which silently inverts the rollout.

Platform.description: <os>-<arch>, produced by the node's detect_platform() and stamped into its runtime manifest.json. Treat as an opaque string and match exactly.

NoUpdate.description: The node is current, or the rollout is deliberately withheld from it. The node treats both cases identically.

channels.description: Channels this node's system has, so the device can turn update.channel into a dropdown of what this server really offers. Flat names, strings only. Present on BOTH response shapes: a node sitting on a channel this server does not have receives the no-update shape forever, and this list is the only thing that can correct it. Includes paused channels. Omitted when the node could not be placed, because then no correct list exists. NOT covered by the signature - see section 7.

UpdateAvailable.description: An offered update. `version` must be strictly newer than the node's `version` by the ordering rule in the Version schema.

url.description: Absolute, or relative to the base URL. May carry its own query string.

size.description: Exact package size in bytes; checked before and after download.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the package. Its value comes from being inside the signed payload — the signature binds the manifest, the manifest binds the bytes.

target.description:
The platform set this artifact covers, canonicalised: one platform for a slim artifact, or every platform in a catalog bundle SORTED ASCENDING and comma-joined with no spaces (e.g. "android-aarch64,linux-x86_64"). Sorting is what lets two implementations derive the same signed string.

The node needs this to rebuild the signed payload, and MUST also confirm its own platform is a member of the set — verifying the signature alone would let an attacker replay a genuine manifest issued for a different platform.

min_version.description: Upgrade floor. If the node's installed version is older than this, it refuses and must step through an intermediate release first.

mandatory.description: Display hint for the front-end only. It does NOT bypass the user: the node always requires an explicit accept, and the server cannot force an unattended restart.

notes.description: Release notes shown to the user before they accept.

channels.description: Channels this node's system has, so the device can turn update.channel into a dropdown of what this server really offers. Flat names, strings only. Present on BOTH response shapes: a node sitting on a channel this server does not have receives the no-update shape forever, and this list is the only thing that can correct it. Includes paused channels. Omitted when the node could not be placed, because then no correct list exists. NOT covered by the signature - see section 7.

system.description: Which product this answer is for. NOT covered by the signature - see section 7.

Signature.description:
Ed25519 over a fixed-order, newline-delimited payload — NOT over the JSON. Canonical-JSON schemes invite two implementations disagreeing about key order and whitespace, and the failure is silent.

payload = version \n size \n sha256 \n target \n min_version \n published_at

Exactly six fields in this order, joined by U+000A, no trailing newline. `size` is a plain decimal integer. `target` is the canonical platform set (see the UpdateAvailable.target schema). An absent optional field contributes the empty string, so the separators remain. Encode UTF-8, sign, base64 the 64-byte signature.

Verification is TWO steps: check the signature, then check that this node's platform is in `target`. See docs/update-server-api.md §7 for a worked example.

key_id.description: Names which public key signed this. Ship nodes a key_id -> public key map so keys can rotate. A node that does not recognise the key_id MUST reject the update, never fall back to trusting it.

value.description: Base64 (RFC 4648, padded) of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature.

error.description: On failure, the node's reason. Existing apply-side codes: sha_mismatch, size_mismatch, failed_to_extract, missing_manifest, no_variant_for_platform, config_reconcile_failed.
Stable machine code the node branches on.

NotModified.description: If-None-Match matched; the node keeps its previous answer.

BadRequest.description: A required query parameter is absent, empty or malformed.

NotFound.description: No such version/platform artifact, or the endpoint is not implemented.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Honour Retry-After and back off.
